sourceArticle.title: How to Build a Scalable Design System in a Monorepo
sourceArticle.author: Vineeth Pawar

athenaOutput.directive: Establish a Sovereign Token-First Compiler Architecture within a Turborepo monorepo, decoupling visual intent from framework execution to ensure absolute multi-platform longevity and zero-dependency bloat.
athenaOutput.rationale: To scale a design system across diverse products without falling into the trap of framework lock-in or fragile dependency chains, we must treat design tokens as the absolute compile-time source of truth. By compiling tokens into framework-agnostic native Web Components and auto-generating lightweight adapters, we fulfill Article I (Sovereignty) and Article IV (Quality Standards) by providing a complete, high-performance, and self-hosted solution that outlasts any single frontend framework lifecycle.

options.title: Sovereign Token-First Compiler Architecture
options.description: Centralize design tokens in JSON/YAML inside a core package, compiling them via Style Dictionary into native Web Components (using Lit) and auto-generating React/Vue adapters. Deployed via a self-hosted Turborepo pipeline.
options.tradeoffs: Requires a higher upfront architectural investment and custom build configurations, but guarantees complete framework independence, absolute sovereignty, and zero runtime performance penalty.

options.title: Multi-Package Monolithic Component Library
options.description: A classic Turborepo setup where components are built as individual React packages (@ds/button, @ds/card) styled with shared Tailwind CSS configurations.
options.tradeoffs: Extremely high developer familiarity and rapid initial velocity, but tightly couples the entire monorepo to React and Tailwind, violating long-term sovereignty if framework migrations are needed.

options.title: Headless + Utility-First Federation
options.description: Publish unstyled headless primitives (e.g., Radix UI, React Aria) alongside a shared Tailwind configuration. Individual applications consume primitives and style them locally using the shared tokens.
options.tradeoffs: Maximum flexibility for application teams and small package sizes, but risks visual drift across apps and makes global design overhauls incredibly difficult to coordinate.

options.title: Zero-Runtime CSS-in-JS (Vanilla Extract) Architecture
options.description: Write type-safe, compiled CSS-in-JS components using Vanilla Extract. Design tokens are mapped to TypeScript variables and compiled to static CSS files during build.
options.tradeoffs: Excellent type safety and developer experience with zero runtime performance cost, but requires complex bundler configurations for every single consumer application in the monorepo.

options.title: Web Components Core with Automated Adapters
options.description: Standardize entirely on native Web Components (using Lit) to ensure complete compatibility across any past, present, or future stack in the monorepo, bypassing framework-specific build toolchains.
options.tradeoffs: Ultimate future-proofing, but introduces complex workarounds for Server-Side Rendering (SSR) environments like Next.js or Nuxt.

options.title: Agentic/AI-Driven Component Generator
options.description: An experimental package that uses local LLMs to dynamically generate React/HTML components on demand based on design tokens and natural language prompts during the build step.
options.tradeoffs: Highly flexible, but completely violates Article IV (Quality Standards) and Article IX (Ship Complete) due to non-deterministic rendering, visual bugs, and extreme build-time unpredictability.
